title: East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship 2027
duration: Up to 24 months; granted one year at a time and renewable
description: The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship provides master's and doctoral degree funding for graduate students from Asia, the Pacific and the United States to pursue study at the University of Hawai'i at Manoa while participating in the Center's residential, educational, cultural and leadership development programs in Honolulu.

title: AAUW International Fellowships
program_type: Graduate fellowship for international women pursuing STEM degrees
description: AAUW's International Fellowships fund international women pursuing graduate study in STEM disciplines in the United States, with the intention of applying their expertise and leadership in service of their home countries. The programme has supported international women in full-time postgraduate study in the United States since 1917. Each award carries a stipend of USD 20,000 for a master's degree or USD 25,000 for a doctorate, disbursed in two equal payments at the beginning and midpoint of the term. title: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) 2027 - Application Window #1 (Developing Country Nationals)
official_source: World Bank, Development Economics Vice Presidency (programme funded by the Government of Japan)
duration: The duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
description: The JJ/WBGSP is a fully funded master's scholarship for mid-career professionals from listed World Bank developing countries who are already admitted to one of a fixed set of participating development-related master's programmes. For the 2027 cycle the World Bank states that a scholarship provides tuition, a monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus, economy class round-trip airfare, basic medical insurance obtained through the university, and a US$600 travel allowance for each trip. title: Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship Program
official_source: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs (administered by the Institute of International Education)
program_type: Merit-based scholarship for U.S. undergraduates to study or intern abroad
description: The Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship Program is a program of the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs that provides up to $5,000 in merit-based scholarships to outstanding American undergraduate students with high financial need to pursue credit-bearing academic studies and career-oriented internships abroad. It is congressionally funded, established by the U.S. Congress in 2001, and administered by the Institute of International Education since its inception. title: Boren Awards (Boren Scholarships and Boren Fellowships)
official_source: Defense Language and National Security Education Office (DLNSEO), National Security Education Program; administered by the Institute of International Education (IIE)
duration: 8 to 52 weeks of overseas study; 25-52 weeks preferred; minimum 12 weeks for most applicants (8 weeks minimum for undergraduate STEM summer programmes).
description: The Boren Awards fund intensive overseas language study for U.S. undergraduate students (Boren Scholarships) and research or language study for U.S. graduate students (Boren Fellowships). They pay a fixed grant of $8,000, $12,500 or $25,000 depending on the duration of overseas study, and the programme states plainly that the award "is not all-inclusive" and is designed to cover only the majority of an awardee's overseas expenses. In exchange, recipients commit to at least one year of federal service in support of U.S. national security after graduation.

title: Phi Kappa Phi Fellowship
official_source: The Honor Society of Phi Kappa Phi
program_type: Fellowship award for first-year graduate and professional students
description: The Honor Society of Phi Kappa Phi awards 40 Fellowships of $8,500 each, six at $15,000 each, and two at $35,000 each to members entering the first year of graduate or professional study. Established in 1932, the Fellowship Program annually provides funding to first-year graduate students pursuing post-baccalaureate degrees across all academic disciplines. Each active chapter may select one candidate from among its local applicants to compete for the Society-wide awards, and endorsed Phi Kappa Phi Fellows go on to study at some of the nation's top graduate schools. title: NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (NSF GRFP)
official_source: U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF), Division of Graduate Education
duration: Five-year fellowship period with three years of financial support
description: The NSF GRFP funds full-time graduate students pursuing research-based master's or doctoral degrees in NSF-supported STEM fields at accredited, nonprofit U.S. institutions. Each fellowship provides three years of financial support over a five-year fellowship period: a $37,000 annual stipend paid to the fellow and a $16,000 annual cost-of-education allowance paid to the institution in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees, so there is no tuition or mandatory-fee cost to the student.
